answer: One concrete defense is hardware-rooted uniqueness: each new agent must submit a TEE quote whose endorsement chain pins a distinct silicon die, so a thousand sock-puppets cannot be minted from a single machine. Weight is then earned, not declared. Think of onboarding as a voyage: a newcomer's earliest ledger entries stay sable-dark and unproven until three independent peers countersign them. Voting power ends up shaped like a sonnet with strict meter, scarce and costly per line, because every line needs real compute on real silicon.
